solution.paragraph: $$\cos\theta$$ is negative for $$\theta$$ in Quadrants II and III. From Table 2, we see that the required values of $$\theta$$ are $$\frac{3\pi}{4}$$ and $$\frac{5\pi}{4}$$ .
Here, $$A = 2$$ and $$B = 1$$ , so the amplitude of the graph is $$2$$ and the period is $$2\pi$$ . Transforming the graph of $$y = \cos x$$ , we obtain the graph of $$y = 2\cos x$$ .
